channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tax Service Warns of New Fraud Schemes Targeting Taxpayers
item.description: The State Tax Service of Kyrgyzstan has alerted taxpayers to new fraud schemes. Scammers may impersonate tax officials, demanding urgent payments or personal data. The service emphasizes that real officials do not request passwords or bank details.

item.title: Russia and Iran Deepen Trade Ties Amid Western Sanctions
item.description: Russia and Iran are expanding cooperation in banking and developing alternative trade routes to counter Western sanctions. Despite challenges like shallow waters and limited port capacity, their trade volume has increased, particularly across the Caspian Sea. This strategic alignment aims to reduce dependence on Western economic systems.

item.title: Kazakhstan Significantly Increases Exports to Brazil, Buys Brazilian Aircraft
item.description: Kazakhstan's trade with Brazil surged 1.7 times in January-August 2026, reaching $339.3 million. Exports, primarily sulfur and fertilizers, grew 2.9 times in value. Kazakhstan also imported meat, sugar, coffee, and notably, two civilian aircraft from Brazil, while imports of engines and car parts decreased.

item.title: Zelensky Open to Meeting Putin in Turkey if Erdogan Organizes
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated he is ready for a hypothetical meeting with Russian leader Vladimir Putin in Turkey, provided Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan can arrange it. Zelensky emphasized the importance of a ceasefire and security guarantees for Ukraine during peace talks.

item.title: Tajikistan's Industry Minister Meets Descendant of Ahmad Donish to Discuss Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Industry and New Technologies, Sherali Kabir, met with Egyptian entrepreneur Odil Donish, a great-grandson of scholar Ahmad Donish. They discussed prospects for cooperation between Tajikistan and Egypt in industry, IT, and AI. The meeting also covered digitalization, mineral extraction, and attracting Egyptian investments.

item.title: Man Illegally Transporting Firearms Discovered in Kyrgyzstan's Nooken District
item.description: A citizen was found illegally transporting firearms without proper permits in a vehicle in the Shaidan area of Nooken District, Kyrgyzstan. Materials were processed, and a fine was imposed for hunting violations. Further investigation into the firearm circumstances is underway by the district's internal affairs department.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov to Visit Talas for New Stadium Opening
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov will undertake a working trip to the Talas region. During the visit, he will meet with residents, hear reports on the socio-economic situation, and attend the opening ceremony of the central stadium 'Talas Arena'.

item.title: OPEC+ Maintains December Oil Production Quotas at September Levels
item.description: Seven leading OPEC+ countries have decided to maintain their current oil production quotas for December at September levels. Experts note that production remains below quotas, with a potential increase in quotas possible in spring 2027 if demand forecasts are met.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Increased Imports of Russian Goods Amid Geopolitical Shifts
item.description: Kazakhstan's imports have risen in the last eight months, totaling five billion dollars, a 6.3% increase year-on-year. Goods from Russia now constitute half of all food imports, with dairy, confectionery, sugar, and grain products notably abundant. This trend is attributed to geopolitical factors limiting Russia's exports to Europe, leading to increased trade within the Eurasian Economic Union.

item.title: Iran States No Decision Made on Changing Nuclear Doctrine Amid War Concerns
item.description: Iran has stated that no official decision has been made regarding changes to its nuclear doctrine, according to Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezai. He indicated that the matter is under discussion, particularly concerning whether to maintain the current doctrine if war recurs. Public sentiment is also a factor, with citizens questioning the doctrine given perceived threats to nuclear facilities.

item.title: Chinese Scientists Set New World Record for Data Transmission Speed
item.description: Chinese scientists have established a new world record for data transmission speed, achieving 3.2 petabits per second over a 24-core optical fiber cable. This speed is equivalent to downloading over 20,000 4K movies in one second. The technology is potentially implementable in the near future.

item.title: Widow of slain Kazakh journalist Aidos Sadykov speaks out on his murder in Kyiv
item.description: Natalia Sadykova, widow of assassinated Kazakh opposition journalist Aidos Sadykov, stated his killing was intended to silence his project. She is raising three children alone in Kyiv under bombardment while continuing her husband's work. The report "Killed. Under Surveillance. Under Trial" was presented in Warsaw.

item.title: US Secretary of State offers to mediate Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions over terror attacks
item.description: The US Secretary of State expressed concern over terrorist attacks against Pakistan originating from Afghan soil. Washington is ready to play a constructive role in easing tensions between the two sides if the opportunity arises, the Secretary stated.

item.title: Turkish President presents Alisher Navoi International Award to Kazakh national
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan presented the Alisher Navoi International Award "For Contribution to the Unity of the Turkic World" to Duesen Kaseinov, a Kazakh statesman, diplomat, and musician. The award recognizes his long-standing contributions to strengthening cultural ties and humanitarian cooperation.

item.title: Kuwaiti Specialists Conduct Nearly 200 Free Surgeries in Karakalpakstan
item.description: Kuwaiti specialists have performed approximately 200 free surgical operations in Karakalpakstan. Medical assistance was provided in cardiology, oncology, ophthalmology, and other fields. The initiative aimed to offer essential medical care to the region's residents.

item.title: Clashes Between Taliban and Pakistani Forces in Paktika Province Result in Casualties
item.description: Local sources report three killed or injured in clashes between Taliban fighters and Pakistani forces in Paktika province. Pakistani forces allegedly launched rocket attacks, destroying homes and causing casualties, including a boy killed and two students injured.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Tokayev Delivers Address Amidst European Protests
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan delivered his address to the Parliament, government members, and invited guests on October 28, 2026. Titled 'Kazakhstan's Current Tasks in a New Historical Cycle,' the speech was published on the Akorda website. The article contrasts current European protests with Kazakhstan's January 2022 events.

item.title: Woman Beaten to Death by Husband in Samangan, Taliban Say
item.description: Taliban police in Samangan province reported that a woman died from injuries inflicted by her husband in the Hazrat-e-Sultan district. The husband has been arrested, and authorities cite family problems as the motive. Domestic violence is reportedly increasing in Afghanistan since the Taliban's return to power.

item.title: Tajik President Inaugurates Two New Enterprises and a Party Building
item.description: On November 1, 2026, Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon opened two industrial enterprises in Buston and a new administrative building for the People's Democratic Party of Tajikistan (PDPT) in Khujand during a working trip to Sughd region. The Buston facility, a livestock and poultry feed producer, was built on the initiative of a local entrepreneur and is equipped with modern technology. The Khujand building will serve as the executive committee office for the ruling party.

item.title: Uzbek Woman with Four Children Rescued from Difficult Situation in Russia
item.description: A group of Uzbek citizens, including a woman with four minor children who faced severe financial hardship in Vladivostok and Khabarovsk, have been repatriated to Uzbekistan. The woman was detained for violating stay regulations. Uzbek consulate officials in Vladivostok and the Migration Agency facilitated their safe return.

item.title: Pakistan Welcomes US Offer to Mediate Afghanistan Talks, Kabul Rejects Allegations
item.description: Pakistan has welcomed a US offer to facilitate dialogue with Afghanistan, stating readiness to support diplomatic efforts to ease tensions. The Foreign Ministry emphasized that meaningful negotiations require verifiable action against militant groups like TTP and BLA operating from Afghan territory. However, Kabul rejected these allegations, asserting that no armed groups are present in Afghanistan.

item.title: Iran-US Negotiations via Qatari Mediators Not Yet Concluded, Says Foreign Minister
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that negotiations between Iran and Qatari mediators regarding an end to the conflict with the US are ongoing but have not reached a definitive conclusion. He indicated that reaching a result depends on the other party's responses to Iran's questions, emphasizing Iran's readiness for both defense and diplomacy.

item.title: Afghan Prime Minister Accepts Credentials of New Belarusian Ambassador
item.description: Mullah Mohammad Hassan Akhund, prime minister of the Islamic Emirate, accepted the credentials of Aleksandr Ogorodnikov, Belarus' non-resident ambassador to Afghanistan. Discussions focused on expanding political, economic, and transit relations. Both sides expressed hope for strengthened cooperation, with Belarus planning to increase trade with Afghanistan.

item.title: Duisen Kaseinov Honored with Alisher Navoi International Award for Turkic Unity Contribution
item.description: Duisen Kaseinov, a prominent figure in Kazakh state and public life, diplomat, and artist, has been awarded the Alisher Navoi International Award for his contributions to Turkic world unity. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan presented the award at the Turkic States Organization summit in Ankara.

item.title: Pilots Honored for Foiling Flydubai Hijacking Attempt
item.description: Two pilots were honored for their bravery in averting a disaster on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A co-pilot attacked the captain with an axe, endangering the 172 people on board. The auxiliary pilots, Stephen Hanson and Rowan Tutt, took control and successfully landed the aircraft in Saudi Arabia. They were awarded the Order of Zayed II by the UAE President.

item.title: New Runway to Be Built at Aktobe Airport, Terminals to Be Reconstructed
item.description: A new runway will be constructed and the passenger terminal reconstructed at the Aktobe International Airport named after Aliya Moldagulova. These projects are part of Kazakhstan's three-year airport development program until 2029. New or upgraded runways are planned for seven airports across the country, with terminal modernizations also underway.

item.title: Taliban Fighters Allegedly Involved in Drug Trade in Zabul Province
item.description: Local sources in Zabul province report that some Taliban fighters are involved with drug traffickers in the collection, processing, and smuggling of narcotics. The sources claim the Taliban do not act against traffickers who share profits but arrest those who refuse. Members of the Counter-Narcotics Directorate and the 205th Corps Brigade are reportedly implicated.

item.title: Belarus Appoints Non-Resident Ambassador to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that Alexander Sirigovich Ugorodnik has been appointed as Belarus's new non-resident ambassador to Afghanistan. The ambassador presented his credentials to the acting Taliban Foreign Minister, Amir Khan Muttaqi, expressing a commitment to developing trade and economic relations between the two countries.

item.title: Pakistan Trade Route Closures Cause Cotton Prices in Helmand to Plummet by 60 Percent
item.description: Helmand farmers report a 60% drop in cotton prices due to the closure of trade routes with Pakistan. Rising costs for fertilizers and pesticides, coupled with poor quality supplies, have increased farming expenses. The closure means harvested cotton remains unsold, preventing farmers from recovering their costs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Vice President Explains Decision Not to Award State Prize
item.description: Yerlan Karin, head of the commission for the Abai State Prize in Literature and Arts, explained the decision not to award the prize in 2026. He stated that the prize is for works, not individuals, and awarding it based on personal preference would not advance art. Karin noted that no submitted work received a clear majority of votes, and a reform of the prize awarding process is needed.

item.title: Kazakh Wrestler Nurkoja Kaipanov Wins Silver at Home World Championship
item.description: Kazakh freestyle wrestler Nurkoja Kaipanov secured a silver medal at the World Championship in Astana. He lost the 74kg final to Russia's Inalbek Sheriev 4:10. Kaipanov was the sole finalist for Kazakhstan across all wrestling disciplines at the home event. This silver medal marks his fourth World Championship medal overall.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened in Aktau After Visitor Assaults Doctor
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in Aktau following an assault on a doctor at the regional children's hospital. The incident occurred in the emergency room when a visitor, after being told his child did not require hospitalization, allegedly attacked the doctor. Security cameras captured the event. Authorities are investigating the circumstances, and the doctor continued working afterward.

item.title: Kazakhstan Court Orders Reconsideration of Afghan Woman's Asylum Request
item.description: A court in Almaty, Kazakhstan, has ordered the Employment and Social Programs Department to reconsider an Afghan woman's asylum application due to new circumstances. Her initial request was denied, but she reapplied citing threats to her and her children's safety. This is the first time a court has mandated a review of a new asylum claim based on changed conditions.

item.title: Roads in Astana to Experience Limited Access November 5-7 for International Events
item.description: Traffic will be restricted on several Astana streets from November 5-7 due to international political events being held in the city. The security measures will involve special state, law enforcement, and armed forces resources. Military aviation training flights will also occur in the capital's airspace starting November 1.

item.title: Georgia Denies Entry to Nearly 500 Uzbek Citizens Since Year Start
item.description: Georgia has denied entry to approximately 500 Uzbek citizens since the beginning of the year. The primary reasons cited include failure to clearly explain the purpose of travel, lack of hotel reservations and return tickets, absence of medical insurance, and insufficient financial means.

item.title: Eight Killed in Gaza Airstrikes, Including Five Police Officers, Health Ministry Reports
item.description: At least eight people, including five police officers, were killed in recent Israeli airstrikes on the Gaza Strip, according to Gaza's Hamas-controlled Interior Ministry and medics. The strikes occurred in Gaza City and Khan Younis. Israel's military stated it targeted militants in Khan Younis but did not comment on the Gaza City strike.

item.title: UN OCHA Warns of Funding Shortages Crippling Healthcare Services in Afghanistan
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports that funding shortages are forcing Afghan healthcare facilities to cut services or close. People in remote areas face long journeys for care. While partners are working to improve access, OCHA stresses that sustained funding is crucial for essential services, maternal, and child health.

item.title: OPEC+ Countries Maintain December Oil Production Levels
item.description: Seven OPEC+ nations, including Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman, have agreed to maintain their September 2026 oil production quotas for December 2026. The decision was made during an online meeting where participants reviewed the global oil market situation.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 102 Service Receives Up to 15,000 Calls Daily
item.description: Kazakhstan's 102 emergency service operators handle between 12,000 and 15,000 calls and messages daily across the country. Since the beginning of the year, police have received over 4.1 million calls. All requests are registered and forwarded for action.

item.title: Taliban Claim Pakistani Forces Attack in Paktika Kills One, Wounds Two
item.description: The Taliban's security command in Paktika province claims Pakistani military forces attacked civilian homes in the Shkin district. The attack reportedly resulted in the death of a young man and injuries to two students. The Taliban stated that financial damages were also inflicted on civilian homes. Pakistani officials have not yet commented.
